root_motivation: Joe's objective is all gates green; today green is a property of the whole checkout and the box, so a clean diff reads red. Evidence: in the 14-day histogram no test, clippy, fmt, or deny receipt is in the top five; `rollback-plan` blocks 147 times on "commits not all revert-clean" for commits already on main; `ci-checks` blocks 157 times mostly on `no-runs-on-ref`/pending; `extended-receipts` is one bit over 17 producers with an 1,800 s wall budget (`EXTEND_GATE_LOOP_WALL_S`, `extend-gate.sh:319`), and 59 blocked gates exceeded 1,500 s. Consequence: a branch's verdict measures the crate and the hour, not the PRD; every re-gate costs 10-28 min of the one build host.
user_persona: The autobuilder skill orchestrator (a Claude session) and the human invoking `/autobuilder` from their own project. Both shell out to this binary for the receipt + gate steps that must not live in bash.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a worktree whose diff adds a failing test, When `--scope branch` runs, Then `verdict=block` names the tests receipt and no `rollback-plan` or `ci-checks` receipt is in `blocks[]`.

Given a worktree with a clean diff on a main whose last three commits are not revert-clean, When `--scope branch` runs, Then `verdict=pass` and `rollback-plan` is listed `not-run class=history-infra`.
Given an extended producer with no class declaration, When the gate runs at branch scope, Then it is `not-run` and journaled `class=history-infra (undeclared)`.

Given a landing whose own commit is not revert-clean, When `--scope main` runs, Then `main-health` has an `in-scope` rollback-plan block and `archive-gate.sh` refuses naming it; given the same block on an older commit, Then archive proceeds and the block is `inherited`.
Given a producer exceeding its per-producer budget, When the gate runs, Then that receipt is `incomplete`, retried once, and the verdict is never `block` on its account.
Given an unchanged tree, When `--scope branch` runs twice, Then the second run is a cache hit under 10 s.

Given the fix landed on RedBaron, When the next mcphost branch gate runs, Then its journal line reports `wall=` under 600 s and `class=tree` receipts only. (Live; evidence: `journal:gate  mcphost-[a-z0-9-]+  (pass|delta-pass|block) .*scope=branch .*class=tree`)
Given a session start after one main-health run, When the banner prints, Then a `main-health:` line with sha, verdict, and age is present.
Given four tree producers and two cargo-budget slots, When the gate runs, Then at most two run concurrently and receipts are written per producer.
Given no landing for 7 h, When the scheduled probe fires, Then `main-health` runs once and journals it.
Given `--what-if <sha>`, When it runs, Then each known block is printed with its class and nothing executes.

scope: Stage 4 risk gate (7 receipts + release receipt)
non_goals: Spawning Claude subagents from the binary itself (that is the orchestrator's job)
Web-service, WASM, or embedded scaffolding (v1 supports cli + lib only)
Auto-applying self-evolution proposals (always gated for user review)
Re-running the underlying audit/test commands inside `gate` (gate only attests; producers own the work)

five_whys_trace.q: Why a Rust companion binary instead of a pure-skill scaffold?
five_whys_trace.a: Shell is too easy to subvert (set -e off, grep eaten, jq missing). The load-bearing parts — metric extraction, digest binding, schema validation — need a typed implementation under tests.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a 7-receipt gate instead of `cargo test && cargo clippy`?
five_whys_trace.a: Each receipt covers a class of failure that the others miss: clippy doesn't see CI status, tests don't see proof-lane routing, and none of them produce an independent-review record. The gate is what makes 'ready' falsifiable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bootstrap autobuilder against itself before running it on other projects?
five_whys_trace.a: If the gate model can't certify the binary that produces gate receipts, it can't be trusted on any other project. The meta-bootstrap is the cheapest adversarial test of the whole pipeline.

five_whys_trace.q: Why deny unwrap/expect everywhere in src/ when most of this is glue code?
five_whys_trace.a: Glue code that panics on a missing receipt or malformed JSON destroys the audit trail at exactly the moments the gate matters most. Erroring back to the caller keeps the diagnostic surface alive.

five_whys_trace.q: Why digest-bind every receipt instead of trusting file timestamps?
five_whys_trace.a: Timestamps lie under git checkout. A self-binding sha256 lets the gate detect tampering and lets reviewers re-verify by recomputing on the receipt's own contents.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the autobuilder repo's 'project' live for the gate — repo root or autobuilder/ workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Repo root. agent/, scripts/, target/autobuilder/ all sit at /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder/. Proof-lanes globs use autobuilder/src/** prefix to match `git diff` output.
